summary: This document clarifies how policy qualifiers may appear in the certificate policies extension of RPKI resource certificates. RPKI certificates tie Internet number resources, such as IP address blocks, to their holders, and this update removes ambiguity left in RFC 6487.

plainLanguage.summary: RPKI resource certificates must contain one policy, and this RFC clarifies that they may also contain one pointer to the issuer's Certification Practice Statement. That pointer cannot change the policy's meaning, and checking it is not required to validate the certificate.

questions: what is a policy qualifier in rpki
subtitle: RPKI resource certificates may include one CPS pointer as a policy qualifier.

tldr.problem: RFC 6487 required one certificate policy but did not clearly say whether a policy qualifier could accompany it.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7318 allows at most one qualifier and requires it to use the CPS pointer type, id-qt-cps. The qualifier must not change the meaning of the RPKI Certificate Policy.
tldr.outcome: This Proposed Standard updates RFC 6487 and brings certificates with the allowed qualifier within its profile.

today: RFC 7318 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 6487. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Unclear Rule
sections.content:
RFC 6487 profiles X.509 certificates used in the Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI). It requires a critical certificate policies extension containing exactly one policy.

RFC 5280 allows that policy to include optional PolicyQualifierInfo objects. RFC 6487 did not say whether those objects were allowed, although it generally bars unlisted fields. Some RPKI certificate authorities needed a clear rule.
sections.plainLanguage: The certificate rules required one policy but did not clearly address an optional item that can go with it. Some certificate issuers needed to know whether they could include that item.

sections.title: The Updated Certificate Rule
sections.content:
The extension remains required and critical, and it must still contain exactly one policy. RFC 7318 adds that exactly one policy qualifier MAY be included.

If present, its policyQualifierId MUST be the Certification Practice Statement pointer type, id-qt-cps. The qualifier MUST NOT change the definition of the RPKI Certificate Policy.
sections.plainLanguage: A certificate may include one qualifier, and it must be a pointer to the issuer's practice statement. The qualifier cannot alter the policy itself.

sections.title: Validation and Security
sections.content:
The qualifier is a URI, but following it is not required for certificate validation. Dereferencing it could cause denial-of-service work at the URI's host; the specification sets no processing requirements for that URI.

A strict validator that implements only RFC 6487 could wrongly reject certificates that follow this update. The security considerations of RFC 6487 also apply.
sections.plainLanguage: Certificate validation does not require opening the URI. A validator that does not know this update might reject a certificate that uses the permitted qualifier.

references.text: Cooper, D., Santesson, S., Farrell, S., Boeyen, S., Housley, R., and W. Polk, "Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure Certificate and Certificate Revocation List (CRL) Profile", RFC 5280, May 2008.
Huston, G., Michaelson, G., and R. Loomans, "A Profile for X.509 PKIX Resource Certificates", RFC 6487, February 2012.
